lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: copying segments and angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Central angle per side?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The construction relies on the angle being acute.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.
The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a line segment?
choices: part of a line that goes on forever in one direction
a line with a measurable length
the set of two endpoints and all points between them on the line through them
the shortest path between two shapes

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. From vertex V draw an arc crossing both rays at P and Q. From P and Q draw equal arcs meeting at R. Draw ray VR. What has been constructed?
choices: the bisector of the angle at V
a line perpendicular to one ray
the perpendicular bisector of PQ only
an equilateral triangle on PQ

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 12. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.
Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: the space between two intersecting lines
the amount of turn measured in degrees
the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
a corner of a polygon

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A regular quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius 2. What central angle does each side subtend?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
